verdict: Version 2 resolves the spreadsheet-versus-records boundary, removes both unjustified prerequisite edges, and gives every root a genuine cross-child synthesis task. One material granularity defect remains before stable leaf-level sampling: calendar scheduling now combines constraint allocation with invitation, recurrence, reminder, cancellation, and historical-state management, while its two probes exercise those capability bundles separately.
findings: Coverage reaches all five C21 guideposts. The ten leaves distinguish spreadsheet structure from calculation, form intake from records organization, document composition from finalization, presentation planning from production, and correspondence from calendar work. All eight discovery tasks use one same-day 10:00-to-16:00 calendar schema and require event identity, duration, accumulated time constraints, and non-overlap; calendar-001, calendar-004, and calendar-008 also require restoration to a named earlier turn. They therefore have a precise home in c21.coordination.scheduling. Version 2 also names dates, recurrence, time zones, invitations, response state, shared resources, reminders, and cancellation, which closes the plausible calendar omissions identified in review_v1 at the outcome level; the discovery set does not supply evidence for those added behaviors.

c21.coordination.scheduling is now too broad for the rubric's predictive-granularity test. Its first probe requires a cross-zone recurring series, a shared room, a holiday exception, and invitations; its second requires historical snapshot restoration, cancellation, response-state handling, a moved event, reminders, and cancellation history. Success on the first state model gives weak evidence of success on the second. Split constrained event placement from calendar lifecycle and state restoration, or narrow the leaf to one shared decisive operation and treat the remaining calendar features as bounded task conditions. A split would keep the hierarchy at depth two and would not require one section per calendar feature.

All five roots satisfy the current cross-child synthesis requirement. The spreadsheet probes combine model structure with formulas and controls; the records probes combine intake design with filing or lifecycle repair; the document probes combine substantive revision with final formatting; the presentation probes combine narrative planning with slide production; and the coordination probes combine a message with a calendar-state change. These roots therefore represent composite trainable outcomes rather than duplicate weighting for a single child.

The spreadsheet-versus-records boundary is repaired. c21.spreadsheets.structure is anchored to existing source data, calculation-ready grain, assumptions, and downstream formula regions. c21.records.capture is anchored to collecting new information through a form, while c21.records.organize is anchored to naming, status, provenance, retrieval, and retirement. Their reciprocal exclusions state these distinctions, and both spreadsheet-structure probes now prepare operational data for later calculations instead of using room reservations as a container-driven proxy for records work.

The empty prerequisite lists are appropriate for the representative tasks. Spreadsheet calculation starts from an existing model, slide production starts from an approved outline or nearly complete deck, and document finalization starts from supplied content. None of those tasks requires mastery of the full sibling outcome. The needed structure, plan, or content is a task input, which follows the rubric more accurately than a hard prerequisite edge.

Every section has two executable instructions that differ in substance. The leaf probes generally share an observable correctness contract, and each root probe exercises both children. The calendar probes are individually instantiable, but their independent feature bundles reveal the scheduling leaf's granularity problem; packing more calendar operations into each instruction would make the probes harder without establishing transfer.

No held-out retrieval or similarity results were supplied. The discovery tasks support constrained placement and, in three cases, prior-turn restoration, but their shared event_id, start_time, and duration state cannot test the new multi-day recurrence, time-zone, invitation-response, shared-resource, reminder, or cancellation claims. Confidence in the other nine leaf boundaries comes from outcomes, exclusions, and probes rather than mapping evidence.

The hierarchy remains compact at five roots, ten leaves, and two levels. The roots earn their place through cross-child synthesis, and the paired leaves under spreadsheets, records, documents, and presentations correspond to distinct generation and evaluation decisions. Adding one calendar-lifecycle leaf would improve sampling coherence at a small size cost; there is no evidence for further calendar-feature sections or another hierarchy level.
rubric_changes: Add a revision regression check to useful granularity: when a coverage fix broadens a leaf, verify that the revised probes still share one decisive operation and correctness contract. If each probe instead covers a different added capability bundle, split the leaf or narrow its outcome.
